transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Thompson, how are you doing today?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am doing alright, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good to hear. Listen, I wanted to come by and talk to you about your MRI scans and the plan for your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: So, there was a bit of a mix-up with the imaging. We had a situation where two different patients had their studies stored under the same accession number.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not sure what that means.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, basically it means the computer filed two different people's pictures in the same folder. Because of that, the surgical team reviewed the wrong scan when they were deciding how to do your procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did I get the wrong one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, but we looked at someone else's images instead of yours. It's sorry for any confusion this caused, but we were just really busy on the imaging floor that day.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think so.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's really just a technicality in the system. Anyway, we've identified the mistake now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel a bit worried about it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the main thing is we have the right images now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it change the surgery?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, it might. We are re-evaluating the approach. Now, since I have to go see another patient in a few minutes, I want to quickly get through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wonder if—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The important part is that we caught it before the actual operation. It's a common kind of system glitch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it dangerous?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're concerned, but we're handling it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter said I should ask about the risks.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I mean, the risk is minimal because we are fixing it now. Let's just wrap this up so I can get back to the ward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: So for the plan, we are going to look at the images again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will that happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime soon. The team will probably be in touch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need to do anything?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not really. Just stay in your bed and wait for us to come back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just a bit confused about who had the other scan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It doesn't really matter who it was, Mr. Thompson. The point is we have your correct MRI now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have a few more things to check on the floor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're welcome. I'll have someone stop by later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will they tell me the new plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see. We'll likely send an update or someone will pop in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I will just lie down then.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sounds good. I'll get going now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('quickly get through this', 'wrap this up', 'get back to the ward') and interrupts the patient's attempt to speak.

E.justification: The error is explicitly named early using lay language and the resident checks for comprehension ('Does that make sense?').

A.justification: A direct apology is offered ('It's sorry for any confusion'), but it is immediately diluted by an excuse regarding being 'really busy on the imaging floor'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but does not name specific emotions or engage with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The plan consists of placeholders and vague timelines ('Sometime soon', 'We'll see', 'someone will pop in').
